title: Impact of Institutional Ownership on Firm Value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Instrumental‐Variables (2SLS).  
Rationale: S&P 500 inclusion (z) shifts institutional ownership (x) exogenously because index funds must hold newly added constituents. We use z as an instrument for x to estimate the causal effect of institutional ownership on firm value (y).

Key assumptions  
1. Relevance – Inclusion in the S&P 500 significantly increases institutional ownership (Cov(z,x) ≠ 0).  
2. Exclusion – Conditional on controls, index inclusion affects firm value only through the change in institutional ownership (Cov(z, u) = 0, where u is the structural error in the y-equation).  
3. Independence/Random assignment – Around the inclusion decision, firms are comparable after conditioning on controls.  
4. Monotonicity – Index inclusion does not decrease institutional ownership for any firm.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# ---- Packages ----
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)       # fast CSV reader
  library(dplyr)       # data manipulation
  library(AER)         # ivreg()
  library(sandwich)    # robust vcov
  library(lmtest)      # coeftest()
})

# ---- 1. Read data ----
dat_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s80_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(dat_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Ensure factors/numeric are as expected
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(z = as.numeric(z))      # make sure z is numeric 0/1

# ---- 2. Descriptive check ----
cat("N =", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Mean(y) =", round(mean(df$y), 4), 
    " Mean(x) =", round(mean(df$x),4), 
    " Mean(z) =", round(mean(df$z),4), "\n\n")

# ---- 3. First-stage: x ~ z + controls ----
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_robust_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1")))
cat("First-stage estimate of z on x =",
    round(coef(fs)["z"], 4), 
    " (robust SE =", round(fs_robust_se["z"],4), ")\n")
# Weak-instrument F-stat
fs_f <- waldtest(fs, . ~ controls, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1"))$F[2]
cat("Robust first-stage F-stat =", round(fs_f,2), "\n\n")

# ---- 4. 2SLS / IV regression ----
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv, vcov = vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1"))

# ---- 5. OLS benchmark ----
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_robust <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))

# ---- 6. Print key results ----
cat("====== MAIN RESULT ======\n")
cat("IV coefficient on institutional ownership (x):",
    round(iv_robust["x","Estimate"],4),
    "  Robust SE:",
    round(iv_robust["x","Std. Error"],4), "\n\n")

cat("OLS coefficient on x:",
    round(ols_robust["x","Estimate"],4),
    "  Robust SE:",
    round(ols_robust["x","Std. Error"],4), "\n\n")

# ---- 7. Sensitivity: Add squared control as robustness check ----
df <- df %>% mutate(controls_sq = controls^2)
iv_rb <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + controls_sq |
                 z + controls + controls_sq, data = df)
iv_rb_robust <- coeftest(iv_rb, vcov = vcovHC(iv_rb, type = "HC1"))

cat("Robustness: IV coef with nonlinear control:",
    round(iv_rb_robust["x","Estimate"],4),
    "  SE:", round(iv_rb_robust["x","Std. Error"],4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative.  
Magnitude: Roughly −0.4 to −0.7 (a one-standard-deviation rise in institutional ownership induced by index inclusion is expected to lower firm value by ~0.4–0.7 standard deviations).  
Reasoning: Passive index investors exert limited monitoring compared with active owners; the mechanical demand can inflate share supply without enhancing governance, leading to a modest decline in valuation when ownership concentration rises through this channel.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use S&P 500 inclusion as an instrument for institutional ownership.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased institutional ownership, driven by index inclusion, leads to a decrease in firm value.
